Same-repo consumer, not release-gated. Dispatch obligation: re-verify the card's file surface on the merged ref — the #11006 landing (`publishMetaItem` optional member, ruled B) may have absorbed or reshaped part of this follow-up; if fully absorbed, close with evidence instead of dispatching.

Container & model: `S`, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus` (tier: `dispatch-gates.mjs --tier packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts` returns **no path-derived mandate**, quoted not recalled. Floor is sonnet and the compile check is mechanical, but the card carries a judgement branch — "if a second, independent reason for the cast surfaces, that is a finding" — and misjudging that branch is how a cast gets silently re-added. Default judgement tier.)
Clause-②: no — this removes a cast that carried *member existence*, not request shape. The accept set does not move in either direction; the declared member already shipped in `packages/spec`. This is `declared = enforced` catching up on the consumer side.
Serial constraints cleared: ⚠️ **PR #11641 is open on this exact file** (`packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts`, card #11546, `domain:cli` seat). **Regions measured disjoint** — its hunks are `@@ -3622,2 +3622,40 @@` and `@@ -3627 +3665 @@`, i.e. the `openapi.json` `info.version` block at ~3619-3665. This card's door is at **5940 / 6051**, ~2300 lines away in a different method. Measured from the diff, ⛔ not from the PR's prose — the region-from-prose mistake is on this seat's record and cost a wrongly-withheld dispatch. Other seats do not stop because this seat holds a file, so the region criterion is the only one that applies to #11641. No other open PR touches this file.

## Premise re-verified on the merged ref — NOT absorbed

The unlock scan's dispatch obligation was to re-verify on the merged ref and **close with evidence if the #11006 landing absorbed this**. It did not. Measured on `origin/main` @ `cad8b42`:

- `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts:2535` declares `publishMetaItem?(request: PublishMetaItemRequest): Promise[PublishMetaItemResponse]` — an **optional member carrying the request type**, which is exactly the shape this card's premise requires (ruled B on #11006, landed via PR #11426). Not a narrowed variant.
- Both cast sites are still live: `(p as any).publishMetaItem` at **5940** (the existence check) and **6051** (the call).
- ⚠️ The handover recorded these at 5916 / 6027. They moved. Line numbers are taken fresh at dispatch, never copied from the card.
- Positive control: 166 occurrences of `as any` in this file, so the zero-elsewhere readings are readings and not a broken matcher.

## What the acceptance signal actually is

Per the card, removing the cast should degrade to the existing optional-call idiom used by `getMetaItemLayered` / `deleteMetaItem`, and with #9741's `TransportScopedMetaRequest` wrapper an undeclared key at the call site becomes a **compile error**. That compile error is the point of the exercise, not a side effect.

⚠️ There is a docblock at ~6029-6031 that exists solely to explain why the cast is there (it names the `TS2339` it would otherwise produce). It is falsified by this change. Leaving it behind would be a declaration that outlived its subject — the same defect class as the sibling card #11222 in this batch.

⛔ `packages/spec` is off limits from this lane. If the cleanup turns out to need anything further in spec, that goes back to the `domain:spec` seat as its own card — ⛔ not into this PR.

## H17 on-hold trigger index — zero intersection

Intersected against all 17 indexed holds on the patrol anchor (#9857). No hit on `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts`.

## ACCEPT — PR #11682

Reviewer of record: `domain:engine` seat, `huangyiirene`, session `session_01VK8rFDtg8eREaxBGX99Csn`. Checked **against the diff and GitHub**, not against the report. ⛔ Landing is held — see the last section.

### Form and scope

| Check | Reading |
|---|---|
| Draft, base `main` | ✅ draft `true`, base `main` |
| Closing keyword | ✅ verified from GitHub's own binding, not by reading the body: this card's `closed_by_pull_requests` resolves to **#11682**. Correct — the card's whole scope is delivered. |
| Path surface (from the diff) | ✅ 2 files: `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts` + `.changeset/rest-publish-meta-item-cast-retired.md` |
| Governed surface | ✅ **none**. Normal landing path. |
| Clause ② | ✅ not triggered — no `packages/spec/src/**` in the diff, claim declared `Clause-②: no`, and the diff agrees: the spec member was *consumed*, never touched. The lane boundary held. |
| Region vs the same-file neighbour | ✅ hunks at **71, 5940, 6024-6064**; PR #11641's are at **3619-3665**. Disjoint, re-measured on the delivered diff rather than on the claim. |

### The acceptance signal, measured

The card named its own acceptance signal: *an undeclared key at the call site becomes a compile error*. That is now delivered and measured rather than asserted — leg 2 of the three-leg typecheck injected an undeclared key and produced:

```
src/rest-server.ts(6059,25): error TS2353: Object literal may only specify known
properties, and 'undeclaredKeyProbe' does not exist in type
'TransportScopedMetaRequest<{ type: string; name: string; ... }>'
```

with leg 1 and leg 3 (fix in place, and after restore) both exit 0 and no diagnostics. The three-leg shape matters: leg 3 proves the mutation left nothing behind, which a two-leg measurement cannot show.

Verified independently in the diff:

- **Both** cast sites are gone — the 501 guard is now `if (!p.publishMetaItem)` and the call is `await p.publishMetaItem(publishRequest)`. Neither was left half-done.
- `TransportScopedMetaRequest` needed no import: it is a **local** type at `rest-server.ts:167`. So the typing is the repo's own #9741 idiom, not a new construct.
- The 501 feature-detection guard correctly **survives** — the declared member is optional, and that guard is also what narrows it to callable. Removing it would have been the plausible-looking mistake here.
- **The stale docblock is replaced, not left behind.** This was the specific thing I asked for, because a rationale that outlived its subject is the same defect class as the sibling card in this round (#11222). The replacement also keeps the counter-intuitive measurement (`TS2339`, not `TS2353`) that explains why only declaring the member could retire this cast.

### The one judgement call — no type-level pin — accepted on a fact I re-measured

The dev deliberately added no `@ts-expect-error` pin, arguing such a pin would be **inert**. That argument is load-bearing, so I checked it rather than accepting it: `packages/rest/tsconfig.json` carries

```
"exclude": ["node_modules", "dist", "**/*.spec.ts", "**/*.test.ts"]
```

So test files in this package are genuinely outside the tsc program, and a type-level pin there would compile nowhere and guard nothing. **A pin nothing compiles is worse than no pin** — it reads as coverage. Accepted. The guarantee is exercised where it *is* compiled (leg 2, in `src/`), and the declaration side is already pinned upstream by #11006.

### Honest limitation, correctly reported rather than papered over

The historic `TS2339` is reproduced from #10350's record and **not** re-measured. That is the right call and I want it on the record as such: re-measuring it would have required reverting the spec member, and `packages/spec` is out of bounds from this lane. Choosing a citation over a boundary breach is the correct trade, and saying so is better than a silent gap.

Also noted, no action: the first `pnpm install` failed on a `better-sqlite3` node-gyp postinstall and the follow-on build reported `tsup: not found`. Environmental, not a code signal, and flagged precisely because that log reads like a real failure. Repo-wide `pnpm lint` was run here (not narrowed), so no narrowing evidence is owed on this PR.

### ⚠️ Cross-read finding — this card's own model is defective

Only visible by reading the card together with what the dev filed, so recording it here. This card's body prescribes the target shape as *"the existing optional-call idiom (matching `getMetaItemLayered` / **`deleteMetaItem`**)"* — it held `deleteMetaItem` up as the model to imitate. The dev's #11679 measures that model: `deleteMetaItem` **is** a declared member, but `DeleteMetaItemRequestSchema` declares only `type` and `name` while the reset door sends **8** members — six of them undeclared and on the wire today.

So the imitated sibling has a genuine request-shape gap that this door no longer has. That does not affect this PR (which followed the *idiom*, not the sibling's schema), but it means the card's framing was optimistic about its own reference point. #11678 is the same family one step further out: `auditMetaItem` is declared **nowhere**, so that door's 4-member literal compiles against nothing. Both are `domain:spec` decisions, both filed unassigned and unlabelled for triage.

### Out-of-scope cards — verified present and correctly shaped

#11678 and #11679 both exist, both unassigned, both unlabelled — neither pre-empts a triage grading.
